A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedCOF research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite changes in title, formatting, and appendix organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated classification results, fine-tuning and linear-probing experiments, and appendix ablations covering feature shift, shrinkage, and noisy statistics.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds prompt-tuning and CCVR comparisons, scatter analyses, and severe-heterogeneity experiments.

M1.justification: The core covariance estimator and within-class classifier remain. v3 removes the separate lambda I regularizer from the stated classifier solve and Algorithm 1, and adds an optional two-stage secure-aggregation adaptation in Appendix I.2. The PDFs do not establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-R, CUB200, Stanford Cars, iNaturalist-Users-120K, and the six-domain DomainNet feature-shift setting. The added comparisons reuse existing datasets; stronger Dirichlet imbalance changes partition settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates PFPT, FedAvg-PT, and FedProx-PT in Table 4. Tables 9–10 also introduce CCVR as classifier initialization and before subsequent FedAdam fine-tuning. v2 cited CCVR but did not evaluate these comparisons; the previous comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds a distinct ViT-B/32 prompt-tuning protocol using 120 rounds, 10 participating clients per round, and fixed or adaptive prompt pools. It also adds conditioning measurements, train-versus-test evaluation, and 100-client experiments with Dirichlet alpha values 0.05 and 0.01. The principal existing benchmark splits and fine-tuning budgets remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing scatter and shrinkage ablations, v3 adds spectral-conditioning analysis, training-accuracy evidence about overfitting, and federated comparisons of between-class, within-class, and combined scatter. Figure 5 adds joint shrinkage/client/mean-count analysis, while Tables 15–16 investigate severe imbalance and its relationship to available class means.

E5.justification: Both versions use three- or five-seed averages and existing uncertainty displays, including standard deviations in the noise experiments. Added comparisons follow these reporting practices; no increased run counts, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: The principal Table 3 values and matched earlier experimental plots are unchanged, but substantial results are added. For example, v3 Table 4 reports CUB200 accuracy of 65.0±0.1 for FedCOF versus 38.6±0.9 for PFPT under its ViT-B/32 setting. Additional results cover CCVR, training accuracy, federated scatter variants, and severe imbalance; these are new comparisons rather than improvements over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The original sample-mean, unbiasedness, scatter-decomposition, and non-iid-bias derivations survive renumbering. Appendix I.2 adds secure-aggregation algebra, but its final equality drops a K/(K-1) factor from the shrinkage term, and its global-mean definition omits the class-count weighting used in Algorithm 1.

C1.justification: v3 adds superiority over federated prompt-tuning to the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, and explicitly claims better-conditioned classifier initialization. The central covariance-from-means contribution and accuracy/communication claims relative to FedNCM and Fed3R retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds conditioning and overfitting explanations for excluding between-class scatter, develops the relationship between available means and estimator quality, and hypothesizes that pre-training mitigates feature shift. It also explicitly acknowledges that FedCOF does not guarantee strong privacy and explains that secure aggregation raises communication to the Fed3R level.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies disjoint multiple-mean sampling with at least two samples per mean, gives dataset-specific totals of communicated means, and supplies detailed communication formulas and prompt-pool settings. These clarify implementation without establishing changes to the earlier sampling experiments. The code URL remains the same, while v2's explicit lambda=0.01 setting is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against FedPFT, federated prompt-tuning, and federated low-rank adaptation, plus citations to covariance-based continual-learning methods. The Nguyen et al. (2020) representation-study citation disappears with the former convergence discussion. The principal positioning around FedNCM and Fed3R remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially revises the abstract and introduction, introduces an explicit contribution list, condenses the preliminaries, and reorganizes experimental headings. Appendices are extensively rearranged and consolidated, including moving privacy material and merging dataset, implementation, and oracle details. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout, with redesigned tables and a side-by-side Algorithm 1. New comparison and ablation tables are added, and Figure 5 expands to three panels. Most existing graphics are reused and relocated; v2's communication-scaling plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through relevant prompt-tuning and CCVR comparisons and provides more informative conditioning and heterogeneity analyses. Its explicit privacy/communication qualification also improves transparency. However, the new optional secure-aggregation derivation contains inconsistent shrinkage and global-mean formulas, weakening its exact-equivalence claim. These localized mathematical problems temper the overall benefit.
